text:
[LCST.4.2.3] **Null propagates — stated on the legal form.** When the source is nullable
and evaluates to `null`, the conversion yields `null`. Because a nullable source requires a
`?` target ([LCST.4.3.1]), this is written **`null::T?` → `null`**. **`null::T` — a bare
target on the `null` literal or any nullable source — is a compile error**, not a runtime
propagation. The runtime propagation of `null` through a fallible cast is specified in
[LNUL].

idris.name: lcst_4_2__cast
idris.note: null::T? is null for every target, the runtime half; a bare null::T is the clause's compile error, which no runtime sees, and a trap in the model (the header's residue).

idris.name: lcst_4_3_4__null_source_converts_to_null
idris.note: null::T? is null for every target.
